method: Dimensions are worked from the trimmed text block outwards, in the chosen unit. Each board is page width plus the square minus the hinge allowance by page height plus twice the square, so the board overhangs the fore edge by the square but stops short of the joint by the hinge allowance. The spine strip spans the text block thickness plus the hinge allowance on each side, plus one board thickness of lap onto each board. The assembled case is twice the board width plus the spine strip, which reduces to twice the page width plus twice the square plus the text block thickness plus twice the board thickness. The covering material adds the turn-in on all four edges, so its width is the case width plus twice the turn-in and its height is the case height plus twice the turn-in. Area is that rectangle, reported in square metres at one million square millimetres and in square feet at 92,903.04 square millimetres per square foot. Values are parsed from plain decimal text and refused when blank, negative, written with an exponent or more than one decimal point, or outside the bounds for the selected unit: page 40 to 400 mm, block 1 to 120 mm thick, square 0 to 20 mm, board 0.5 to 6 mm, hinge 0 to 20 mm and turn-in 5 to 40 mm, with separate inch bounds. Lengths are reported to two decimals, square metres to six and square feet to four. The page computes in the browser, stores nothing and makes no network requests.

sources.title: Case binding: the boards of a hardcover case overhang the text block by the square at head, tail and fore edge, and are joined by a spine strip across the joint.
Bookbinding practice: the joint or hinge is the groove where each board meets the spine, and the covering material turns in around every board edge.
International yard and pound agreement: one inch is exactly 25.4 millimetres.
